notes.summary: Index numbers show the relative change in prices, quantities or values compared to a base period (index = 100). JSO asks on simple and weighted indices (Laspeyres, Paasche, Fisher), the tests an index should pass, and uses such as deflating and base shifting.

concepts.title: Simple indices
concepts.body:
• Price relative = (p1/p0) × 100.
  • Simple aggregative = (Σp1/Σp0) × 100.
  • Simple average of relatives = Σ(p1/p0 × 100)/n.
  • The base year index is always 100.

concepts.title: Weighted indices
concepts.body:
• Laspeyres (base-year quantities): Σp1q0/Σp0q0 × 100. Tends to overstate change (upward bias).
  • Paasche (current-year quantities): Σp1q1/Σp0q1 × 100. Tends to understate.
  • Fisher = √(Laspeyres × Paasche). Called the ideal index: it satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
  • Marshall–Edgeworth uses (q0 + q1) as weights.

concepts.title: Tests and uses
concepts.body:
• Time reversal: P01 × P10 = 1. Factor reversal: P01 × Q01 = V01 (value ratio). Circular test: met by simple aggregative and fixed-weight indices, not by Fisher.
  • Real wage = (money wage / CPI) × 100 (deflating).
  • Base shifting: new index = (old index / old index of new base year) × 100.
  • Chain index uses link relatives and is good for long periods.

varieties.name: Simple indices
varieties.how: Divide current by base and multiply by 100.

example.q: Price of rice was ₹40 in 2015 and ₹52 in 2024. Find the price relative (2015 = 100).

varieties.name: Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher
varieties.how: Make columns p0q0, p1q0, p0q1, p1q1, add them, then apply the formulas.

example.q: Laspeyres = 125 and Paasche = 121. Find Fisher's index.

varieties.name: Tests, deflating and base shifting
varieties.how: Remember which index passes which test; for real wage divide by CPI/100.

example.q: A worker earns ₹24,000; CPI is 120. Find the real wage.

tips: Laspeyres → base quantities (q₀); Paasche → current quantities (q₁). "L" comes before "P", base comes before current.
Fisher lies between Laspeyres and Paasche.
CPI is used to find real wages and dearness allowance.
traps: Fisher's index does NOT satisfy the circular test.
Real wage divides by the index, then multiplies by 100.
Laspeyres uses base-year weights even for the current-year prices.

formulas.name: Base shifting
formulas.expr: (Old index / old index of new base) × 100

questions.q: The index number for the base year is always:
questions.solution: The base period is the point of comparison, so its index is taken as 100.

questions.q: The sum of prices of a group of goods is ₹120 in the base year and ₹150 in the current year. The simple aggregative price index is:
Which index number satisfies both the time reversal test and the factor reversal test?
questions.solution: Fisher's ideal index √(L × P) satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests. Laspeyres and Paasche satisfy neither.

questions.q: For the same data (A: p<sub>0</sub> = 10, q<sub>0</sub> = 5, p<sub>1</sub> = 12, q<sub>1</sub> = 6; B: p<sub>0</sub> = 8, q<sub>0</sub> = 10, p<sub>1</sub> = 10, q<sub>1</sub> = 8), Fisher's ideal price index is approximately:
A worker's monthly wage is ₹30,000 and the consumer price index (base = 100) is 150. His real wage is:

flashcards.back: Laspeyres: base-year q₀. Paasche: current-year q₁.
√(Laspeyres × Paasche); passes time and factor reversal tests
